relevance_note: Case series of three children with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants described individually: "Genetic testing showed that all three patients had heterozygous mutation in TNFAIP3 gene."
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and mapped each typed quote onto the exact substring of the Markdown (the paper uses thin spaces U+2009 inside numbers and variant strings); no table was transcribed by script. Table 1 has patients as columns (headers 'Patient1', 'Patient2', 'Patient3'); its spans run from the row label through that patient's cell. Table 2 has patients as rows. The '–' cells in Tables 1 and 2 and the 'N' cells in Table 2 are not defined anywhere in the paper, so they were treated as not reported (no exclusions taken from them); '+' cells were used as present. SCOPE: 3 patients plus 6 parents. Parents of Patients 1 and 2 are included as tested relatives (Methods: blood 'collected from each child and their parents'; Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 captions show gene-mutation maps of each patient's father and mother; their variants were 'confirmed by Sanger sequencing as spontaneous mutations', recorded as de novo); these four parents and the father of Patient 3 (did not carry the mutation) have no variant rows. The mother of Patient 3 carries the variant and is affected. The Discussion's literature summary (24 articles, 35 patients, 14 families) is group-level only and got no rows. LABELS: 'Patient 1/2/3' (the third case's heading is 'Case 3', but 'patient 3' is the more frequent form). AGES: only age at admission is printed; it is recorded as age at last evaluation (follow-up continued for 3-4 months afterwards); onset is recorded as the relative time written ('Six months before admission' etc.) without ISO conversion because it is not an age; no age at diagnosis is stated. is_proband is null for the three patients (the paper does not use 'proband' or 'index case'). vital_status 'alive' is taken from current-status statements. History negatives tied to a time point (e.g. 'There was no fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, rash, eye discomfort.') are recorded as excluded with the time context in severity_or_detail, except where the same feature appears later in the history (Patient 1 fever and bloody stool; Patient 3 abdominal pain), which is a sequence in time rather than a contradiction, so only the observed row is kept. Narrow absences ('rash', 'eye discomfort', 'no ... gastrointestinal symptoms', ANA-only negative for Patient 1) were not used to exclude composite checklist items; Patient 3's negative ANA and ANCA panels exclude 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)', and Patient 3's 'no ... joint swelling and pain' (at onset) excludes 'arthritis or arthralgia'. In silico findings (GERP++ conservation, absence from population databases) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Only c.1906 + 1G > C is classed by the authors ('may affect the alternative splicing'). The pathogenicity wording 'possibility of pathogenicity at genetic level' refers to all three patients' variants and is also given on the mother's row for the same variant. CONTRADICTIONS/INCONSISTENCIES IN THE PAPER: (1) Patient 1 is a 'girl' (her/she throughout, and Methods '1 male, 2 female' with Patient 3 the boy) but the examination sentence says 'a 91 cm and 11.5 kg boy'; recorded female. (2) Patient 1's variant is 'c.925-927dup' in the case text and 'c.925_927dup' in Results; the case-text form is recorded. (3) Patient 3 CRP is 105 mg/L in the text but 17.5 mg/L (prior treatment) in Table 2. (4) Patient 2 ANA titre is 1:100 and later 1:1000 in the text but 1:320 in Table 2. (5) Patient 2's local-hospital CRP (42.7 mg/L) and AESR (50 mm/60 min) are identical to Patient 1's local-hospital values, a possible copy error. (6) Table 1 gives Patient 2 'Renal damage +', but the text says urine tests and 24-h urinary protein were normal and renal biopsy was not performed (Table 2 urine cell '–'); both rows are emitted. (7) Figure captions do not match the text's figure citations (text cites Fig. 3 for Patient 2's spinal MRI and Figs. 4 and 5 for the gene maps of Patients 2 and 3; the captions give Fig. 3 = Patient 2 gene map, Fig. 4 = Patient 3 gene map, Fig. 5 = CT/MRI). (8) The Discussion says steroids were not used in two of the three patients, yet Patient 2 received oral methylprednisolone for 6 months, and it also says 'Most patients still required low-dose steroid therapy'. (9) The abstract says Patient 1 was followed for four months; the case text says adalimumab for 3 months. Patient 2's 'no ... joint swelling' alongside axial spinal arthritis was not treated as a contradiction (peripheral swelling vs spinal arthritis); both rows are kept.
